claim: TSMC said in February 2019 that a batch of problematic photoresist that affected 12/16 nm wafers at Fab 14B would cut its Q1 2019 revenue by about US$550 million, with the scrapped wafers made up in Q2 (adding about US$550 million to Q2 revenue).
evidence: "This incident is expected to reduce Q1 revenue by about US$550 million, gross margin by 2.6 percentage points..." "The wafers scrapped in Q1 will be made up in Q2. This will contribute about US$550 million to Q2 revenue" (TSMC press release, 15 Feb 2019)

metric.name: Expected Q1 2019 revenue impact of Fab 14B photoresist incident
metric.methodology: Company guidance update; revenue deferral, not an audited loss figure

notes: Corrects CLM-1819: the US$550m was TSMC's expected Q1 revenue reduction (mostly recovered in Q2), not the value of scrapped wafers as the European Commission phrased it. FY2019 impact guided at -0.2 pt gross margin and NT$0.08 EPS.

claim: METI's amended certification of SUMCO's 300 mm silicon wafer supply-assurance plan (27 March 2026) cut required funds to ¥58bn and the maximum subsidy to ¥19.3bn, from ¥225bn and ¥75bn.
evidence: "変更認定の日付 令和８年３月２７日" ... "取組を実施するために必要な資金の額：580 億円（最大助成額：193 億円）" (METI certification summary 2023半導体第11号-2); earlier: SUMCO row "2,250 | 750" (SRC-0606, METI May 2024, p. 11)

metric.name: Maximum METI subsidy for SUMCO 300 mm wafer plan (amended)
metric.population: Required funds ¥58bn (580 oku yen); supersedes ¥225bn/¥75bn approval
metric.methodology: METI certification summary under the Economic Security Promotion Act

claim: Under METI's March 2026 amended plan, SUMCO's subsidised 300 mm high-precision wafer capacity is at Yonezawa (crystal, 58,000/month equivalent from January 2028), Kuhara (crystal 58,000/month equivalent from November 2030; processing 125,000/month from March 2031) and Imari Nagahama (processing 94,000/month from March 2031), largely by converting existing lines.
evidence: "米沢工場（結晶） 2028 年１月 5.8 万枚/月相当"; "久原工場（結晶） 2030 年 11 月 5.8 万枚/月相当"; "久原工場（加工） 2031 年３月 12.5 万枚/月"; "伊万里（長浜）工場（加工） 2031 年３月 9.4 万枚/月"; "（※）既存ラインの転用による高精度品の量産"
notes: Replaces the schedule in CLM-1857 (crystal 200k/month-equivalent and wafers 100k/month from Oct 2029 at Imari/Yoshinogari).

claim: Saga Shimbun reported that SUMCO announced on 27 March 2026 a temporary postponement of its planned new plants including in Yoshinogari, Saga, prioritising upgrades of existing plants such as Imari; SUMCO said it would keep studying the new-plant plan.
evidence: "SUMCO（本社・東京）は27日、吉野ヶ里町などへの工場新設計画を一時延期し、伊万里市などの既存工場の製造設備の高度化を優先することを発表した。...工場新設については「計画の検討は継続する」としている。"
notes: Tier-3 news; consistent with METI's amended certification (s_meti26), which no longer lists Yoshinogari.
